lamport_timestamps_simulator.title: Lamport Timestamps Simulator
lamport_timestamps_simulator.subtitle: Visualize how logical timestamps are updated in a distributed system
lamport_timestamps_simulator.info: Add local events or send messages between processes to see how Lamport timestamps are updated. Observe how event ordering is preserved through logical clocks.

consensus.step_initial_raft_desc: All nodes start as followers in term 0.
consensus.step_timeout_election_desc: Node 2 detects that there is no leader and starts an election, becoming a candidate.
consensus.step_vote_request_desc: The candidate (Node 2) requests votes from the other nodes.
consensus.step_receive_votes_desc: The other nodes vote for the candidate if they have not voted in this term.
consensus.step_leader_elected_desc: Node 2 receives a majority of votes and becomes the leader.
consensus.step_log_replication_desc: The leader adds a log entry and replicates it to all followers.
consensus.step_commit_desc: The entry is committed when a majority of nodes record it.
consensus.step_initial_paxos_desc: Initial configuration with a proposer, acceptors, and a learner.
consensus.step_paxos_1a_desc: The proposer sends prepare messages to the acceptors.
consensus.step_paxos_1b_desc: Acceptors send a promise if they have not already promised a higher proposal number.
consensus.step_paxos_2a_desc: The proposer sends the proposed value to the acceptors.
consensus.step_paxos_2b_desc: The acceptors accept the value and notify the learner.
consensus.step_initial_zk_desc: Initial configuration with a leader and followers.
consensus.step_watch_desc: A participant registers an interest in changes.
consensus.step_update_desc: The leader propagates an update to the followers.
consensus.step_notify_desc: The leader notifies the participant about the change.

two_phase_commit_simulator.title: Two-Phase Commit Simulator
two_phase_commit_simulator.intro: This simulator demonstrates the Two-Phase Commit protocol in a distributed bank transfer. Configure bank responses by clicking them before starting the simulation.

steps.s0: Click the banks to configure their responses, then start the simulation
steps.s1: Phase 1: Coordinator sent 'prepare' to all participants
steps.s2: Phase 1: Participants replied with their votes
steps.s3: Phase 2: Coordinator made the final decision
steps.s4: Simulation finished! You can reset to run again.

algorithms.title: Synchronization Algorithms
algorithms.intro: There are several algorithms to ensure synchronization in distributed systems. Each has specific characteristics and ideal use cases.
algorithms.key_concept_text: The choice of synchronization algorithm depends on factors such as number of nodes, network latency, fault tolerance, and performance requirements.

bakery.title: Bakery Algorithm
bakery.concept_p: Based on a bakery where each customer receives a ticket number and is served in increasing order.

token_ring.title: Token Ring
token_ring.concept_p: A token circulates among processes in a logical ring, and only the process holding the token can access shared resources.

ricart_agrawala.title: Ricart-Agrawala
ricart_agrawala.concept_p: Based on logical timestamps, where processes request permission from all others before accessing shared resources.

availability_zones_simulator.title: Availability Zones Simulator
availability_zones_simulator.intro: Explore how availability zones work together to ensure high availability and fault tolerance.

service_oriented.title: Service-oriented design
service_oriented.intro: Explore different approaches to organizing services and their practical implications. Each architecture has trade-offs and suitable use cases.

monolithic.name: Monolith
monolithic.description: All features live in a single codebase, with tight coupling between modules.
advantages: Easier to test end to end
disadvantages: Difficult to scale individual parts of the system
Every change requires a full redeployment
Can become complex as it grows
monolithic.example: A simple online store with catalog, user, and order features in one codebase.

details.deployment: One deployment for the whole application
One deployment for the whole application
One deployment for the whole application

modular.name: Modular monolith
modular.description: Code is organized into well-defined modules with clear boundaries, within one deployment.
advantages: Well-organized modular code with clear boundaries
Easier migration to microservices in the future
A useful balance between simplicity and organization
disadvantages: Still requires discipline to preserve module boundaries
Scalability is still limited by a single deployment unit
Developers may be tempted to bypass module boundaries
modular.example: An online store divided into independent catalog, order, and user modules. Each owns its rules and data, but all deploy together as one application.

details.database: Separate schema in a shared database
Separate schema in a shared database
Separate schema in a shared database

microservices.name: Microservices
microservices.description: Independent services communicate over the network, each with its own deployment and database.
advantages: Flexibility to scale individual parts of the system
Each team can focus on one service
microservices.example: An online store with separate payment, inventory, and user microservices.
